findings: AMBIGUOUS - who takes the first turn in round 2+: Setup §3 step 6 says 'the player to the Locksmith's left takes the first turn,' but this line sits only in the initial Setup list. The 'Between rounds' reset paragraph (end of §3) lists what resets (time rail, Locksmith lane, cut rail, shutters, seat passes left) but never explicitly restates 'then left-of-Locksmith goes first' for round 2 onward. Reasonable to infer it repeats, but the text never says so.

Re-read required on the reading algorithm: the worked example in §5 ('Pins: 3 7 2 5 1 / Key: 3 7 4 5 1 → Reading: 2') needed a second pass to confirm the reading is an unbroken run from chamber 1 and ignores any later accidental matches (chambers 4-5 also matched but don't count).

Re-read required on §4 steps 3-4: had to cross-check 'Locksmith income... happens on a Hold as well as on a failed Probe' against 'After a Hold they may not [re-pin]' to separate the two effects (income yes, re-pin window no) for a Hold.

The text's own teach-time claim ('about 5 minutes to teach') looks optimistic for first-time players: the staircase-cam reading rule, the Probe/Hold/Re-pin economy, and the 4-step tiebreak each need a physical demo, not just a read-through. ~15 min (5 core concepts x ~2 min explain+demo, plus the 2 re-reads above) is more realistic for 3 friends who've never held the lock.

All other tested rulings were directly answerable with citations: pin-rung exhaustion in the case (§8, 'take a different rung... hard limit'), voided round on empty/double-pinned chamber (§8), jam handling (§5 Probe rulings), detent-miss becoming a Hold on second failed attempt (§5), last-turn OPEN resolving before the +5 (§8 Timing), the 4-step tiebreak guaranteeing a single winner (§7), and 2p/3p/4p round-count and Locksmith-frequency rules (§3.5, §8).
